column3: NASB has no “now,” like the critical text; it adds “Him.”
NASB renders “The Christ” as “this Christ” and “upbraiding” as “insulting.”
NASB follows the critical text; the cry and its translation are in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“Behold”); “those having stood by” is rendered “the bystanders.”
NASB follows the critical text; “vinegar” is rendered “sour wine,” and “Wait!” is omitted.
NASB follows the critical text without “having cried out”; “from opposite of Him” is rendered “right in front of Him.”
NASB follows the critical text; “the least” is rendered “the Less.”
NASB adds “women” and renders the imperfects as “used to follow … minister.”
NASB follows the critical text; “having boldness” is rendered “gathered up courage.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the body”).
